name: STIHL MS 362
blurb: 18″, 20″ and 25″ bars on 3/8″ chain, .050″ gauge, 66–84 drive links, per STIHL's chain-selection chart.
intro: The STIHL MS 362 appears in STIHL's saw-chain selection chart with 18″, 20″ and 25″ guide bars: 3/8″ pitch at .050″ gauge. STIHL's chart lists this saw in a block shared with larger saws that also show heavier .063″ chain options, so confirm the gauge on your stamp. If your bar stamp reads .063″ rather than .050″, STIHL's code for the loop changes from 33 RS3 to 36 RS3: same pitch, but a thicker drive link that is made for a .063″ groove and will not seat in a .050″ one. File size is where STIHL and Oregon disagree: STIHL’s 2025 catalog file table lists a 13/64″ (5.2 mm) round file for 3/8″ chain, while Oregon’s filing chart gives 7/32″ (5.5 mm) for its standard 3/8″ chain (72, 73, 75), so the table shows both.

bars.note: STIHL's chart lists chain 33 RS3 66 with recommended bar 3003 008 8917.
STIHL's chart lists chain 33 RS3 72 with recommended bar 3003 008 8921.
STIHL's chart lists chain 33 RS3 84 with recommended bar 3003 000 4030. This longer bar is an exchangeable-nose (RS) type.

sources.title: Saw Chain Selection and Identification (STIHL USA catalog page 173; specifications as of 1 October 2017): recommended chain loop and guide bar per saw model
STIHL 2025 Full Line catalog: Saw Chain Selection and Identification chart (catalog pages 166–167), chainsaw spec tables, saw chain and file pages
Saw Chain Filing Angles / Grinding Angles chart (2020): 7/32″ round file for standard 3/8″ chain (types 72, 73, 75)

sources_note: STIHL USA “Saw Chain Selection and Identification” chart (catalog page 173, specifications as of 1 October 2017), read on 24 Oct 2026. Rows re-checked against the STIHL 2025 Full Line catalog chart (catalog p. 166), which lists the same loops and bar numbers, on 3 Nov 2026. File sizes for 3/8″ rows: STIHL 2025 Full Line catalog file table (catalog p. 167: 5.2 mm / 13/64″ file for 3/8″) and Oregon Saw Chain Filing Angles chart (2020: 7/32″ for 72, 73, 75), both read 3 Nov 2026.
